races.name: Napoleons Casino Hull Dine In Style From £35 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Connexin Ultrafast Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fozzie
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over 7-10f on good, but a natural hold-up type whose trainer Kevin Ryan sends him here fresh at 14 days; the midfield map position is not his natural ground — he sits there because the rear is full, and his chance is shaped by whether he can get a clean run from a compromised berth.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two starts for Charlie Johnston, both on good ground, placing second once over 7f; an unknown quantity but the step up to 7½f and his OR of 120 suggest Johnston expects improvement and he is well respected in this shape.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runner who sports headgear and has placed on good ground over 7-8f; a prominent style suits this race shape well and he represents one of the better chances if Bee Farmer sets an uncontested pace that suits front-rank trackers.

runners_data.name: Wats On Tiger
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with no published form and an unknown going preference — complete wildcard for Brian Rothwell; the extra weight burden of 142lbs is notable and form assessment is impossible, making him a dangerous unknown rather than a confident selection.

runners_data.name: Bee Farmer
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for Edward Bethell ridden by PJ McDonald; won once over 8f on good and has the race entirely on his own terms if allowed to stride on, though the STYLE_FIT tag flags he is mapped slightly out of a naturally pure lead role and should be watched for whether he truly commits to the front.

runners_data.name: Elias Escape
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey runner who has run twice on good ground without placing, both times held up; Warren Fentiman takes the 3lb claim but the hold-up style needs a strong pace to produce an effective late run and that is the least likely scenario here.

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas entry returning after a 150-day break, all form on standard going with no good-ground evidence, and a hold-up style that depends on a gallop this field is unlikely to generate; the layoff and going question make this a significant risk.

runners_data.name: Race To The Edge
runners_data.note: Roger Varian has 10 winners from 32 runners in the last 14 days, a strong yard signal; lightly raced with placed form over 7f on good, and an unknown style tag leaves him tactically flexible — the yard's in-form flag is the main reason to take him seriously.

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop sends this hold-up type back on good ground after 35 days; placed once over 7f on standard, never won, and the style demands a pace that is unlikely to materialise here, making his task uphill in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Bee Farmer is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to bowl along at a measured, self-selected gallop on good ground over 7½f at Beverley. The hold-up contingent — Fozzie, Elias Escape, Lorca's Waltz, and Melting Snow — will be anchored toward the rear, meaning the race is likely to be run at a controlled rather than searching tempo. The field does hold more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Fozzie, a natural hold-up horse, has been mapped to midfield because the rear is congested, though Fozzie is unlikely to command that role freely in this shape. A single uncontested front-runner dictating at a comfortable pace over this stamina-testing Beverley track strongly favours horses racing prominently or from midfield with enough cruising speed to track Bee Farmer, rather than pure closers who will need a strong gallop to reel in a horse in a rhythm.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bee Farmer Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer is allowed to control the pace throughout with no rival forcing the tempo.
scenarios.body: If Bee Farmer is allowed to control the pace throughout with no rival forcing the tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Racer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that Bee Farmer ties up inside the final furlong, allowing a midfield tracker to pick up.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just strong enough that Bee Farmer ties up inside the final furlong, allowing a midfield tracker to pick up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer goes off too hard early and the pace collapses, creating a fast-finishing opportunity.
scenarios.body: If Bee Farmer goes off too hard early and the pace collapses, creating a fast-finishing opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer is headed or refuses to dominate, turning the race into a muddling sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If Bee Farmer is headed or refuses to dominate, turning the race into a muddling sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Bee Farmer (PJ McDonald) — watch the opening quarter-mile to confirm he jumps and establishes the lead unchallenged; if anything pressures him early, the entire pace map shifts.

Wats On Tiger — no form, heaviest weight in the race at 142lbs, and Brian Rothwell has only 2 runners in the last 14 days; this runner is a complete unknown and could behave unpredictably in the early stages.
Lorca's Waltz — 150 days off, no form on turf that translates to good ground, and a hold-up style; a non-trivial risk of underperforming well below market expectations if ring-rusty.

Race To The Edge (Roger Varian, T14: 10/32) — the trainer's 14-day strike rate is the highest in this field; watch for this lightly raced type to be better than his form suggests, particularly if Bee Farmer sets a generous tempo.

Fozzie — watch whether Shane Gray positions him closer than his natural hold-up style demands; if the jockey elects to take a forward position to compensate for redistribution, Fozzie's chance improves markedly over what his mapped midfield slot implies.

races.name: Biffa North Handicap

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the ride on this 4yo who has struggled for consistency in recent outings, and though his good-ground form offers some hope, he is a natural hold-up horse who will find himself racing further forward than ideal in this congested field — discount his chance unless he can patiently find a clear run from midfield.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4yo has placed form over this course and distance on good ground and rides prominently, making this trip and conditions a fair match; Faye McManoman claims no weight allowance but the horse's natural prominent style fits a race where tracking the leader is a genuine tactical option.

runners_data.name: Billyjoegold
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4yo showed a worrying tendency to fade in the finish last time, and though recent form at this trip on similar ground is acceptable, this is a horse whose natural hold-up style means it will likely be operating from further forward than it prefers — the finishing-fade flag is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's 4yo has a modest record on good ground with no wins or places from three relevant efforts, and as a genuine hold-up horse forced into a midfield berth by the cluster of closers in this race, the tactical disadvantage compounds an already uninspiring profile on this going.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 4yo has headgear noted and holds some placed form on good ground at comparable trips, but a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes in recent starts tells its own story; bumped into midfield by the redistribution effect, the horse needs a pocket-friendly run that a 14-runner field may not provide.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's 7yo landed a 7f win on soft ground and retains some ability at this sort of trip, though her record on good specifically shows limited success — she is the most credible of the hold-up types given her course and distance experience, and Tom Eaves' local knowledge is a minor positive.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner with no challenger for the lead, Ruth Carr's 5yo has a strong record of placing at this track and trip on good ground, and James Sullivan can simply roll along uncontested — the uncontested lead is the single biggest tactical advantage in this race and should not be underestimated.

runners_data.name: Oselton
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's 4yo won over 7f on standard ground and placed over this trip on soft, so the step back to good is a slight question mark, though Shane Gray's experience is useful; a natural hold-up type who may actually get a reasonable run from midfield if the early pace strings the field out.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 4yo is fitted with a tongue strap and Harry Davies rides, with a recent 4th on good ground over 7f providing some relevance; a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the field's composition, and while Appleby's 14-day form is solid (2/14), this horse rarely converts its placings into wins.

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: A 10yo veteran fitted with a tongue strap and cheekpieces, trained by Michael Dods who has decent 14-day stats, but a sequence of 8th, 10th, 13th, and 12th in recent starts on good ground makes it hard to see where a winning run comes from — the redistribution into midfield is an irrelevance given the overall form picture.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's 7yo carries headgear and connects to a trainer with an active yard (3/7 in 14 days), but a string of 5ths, 6ths, and 7ths in similar handicaps on comparable ground suggests a horse that competes without threatening; naturally a hold-up type, it will need the race to fall perfectly to figure.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's 3yo holds a 7f win on soft ground but has since finished 8th and 9th on similar ground, and the finishing-fade flag is a concern; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim offers weight relief but the horse's pattern of weakening late makes a genuinely contested mid-division finish its best realistic outcome.

runners_data.name: Crystal Aurora
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 3yo placed over 8f on good ground and shows reasonable form figures, but Robbie Downey takes the ride on a horse that has never won on good turf; from a hold-up position, she needs the race to be run at a pace that creates enough of a gap for a sustained late run, which the controlled front-runner makes less likely.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo is lightly weighted, won over 7f on good ground two runs ago, and Jake Dickson's 7lb claim helps the handicap burden further; a naturally prominent racer who can sit just off Emerald Army's lead, this profile — forward-travelling, in-form, and well-weighted — suits the race shape as well as any horse in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Army is the sole confirmed front-runner and, crucially, faces no identified challenger for the lead, meaning James Sullivan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any pressure forcing the tempo artificially high. Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy are the only other horses with prominent inclinations and may track up behind Emerald Army, but neither is likely to chase hard enough to compromise the pace-setter's rhythm over 7½f on good turf. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up horses — Bantz, Valsharah, Summer Rain, Indy's Angel, Langholm, and Elettaria are all natural closers who cannot all secure their preferred rear position, meaning several will be shuffled into midfield against their natural grain, reducing the effectiveness of the late-running brigade. This race shape, with a single uncontested leader setting a measured tempo and a cluttered midfield of horses racing out of role, heavily favours front-runners and prominent racers able to husband their energy and quicken from a position of advantage into the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Emerald Army Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Army is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip without any rival forcing the pace, controlling the race from start to finish.
scenarios.body: If Emerald Army is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip without any rival forcing the pace, controlling the race from start to finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Line
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy track Emerald Army closely and the pace proves strong enough to stretch the field, opening a gap between the prominent horses and the closers.
scenarios.body: If Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy track Emerald Army closely and the pace proves strong enough to stretch the field, opening a gap between the prominent horses and the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Bridge The Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is set fast enough by the wider field forcing Emerald Army's hand, or the good ground rides particularly quick, allowing genuine closers to run them down.
scenarios.body: If the early tempo is set fast enough by the wider field forcing Emerald Army's hand, or the good ground rides particularly quick, allowing genuine closers to run them down.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and a bunched finish develops, making the form book largely redundant.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses mid-race and a bunched finish develops, making the form book largely redundant.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army leads unchallenged — watch whether James Sullivan is allowed to bowl along completely uncontested, because if no rival challenges in the first two furlongs, the race could be decided before the turn.

Lope Y Linda is the most dangerous horse to Emerald Army's plan — watch whether Jake Dickson elects to sit tight just off the leader or allows a gap to open, as the choice will shape the entire race outcome.

With six genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield, watch for severe traffic congestion on the turn — any horse attempting to deliver a run from the middle of the field faces a genuine routing problem at Beverley's tight home bend.

Oselton's going preference (soft or standard) versus today's good ground is worth monitoring — if he travels comfortably in the first half mile, he becomes the most credible late challenger; if he labours early, discount him quickly.

Miss Willows, despite hold-up tendencies, has course and trip experience and won last time out — watch whether Tom Eaves positions her more prominently than her style tag suggests, as an adjusted tactical ride could bring her into the picture.

races.name: Coachman Caravans Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Recent Beverley good-ground winner over 6f, drops back to 5f here and races as the lone confirmed front-runner; Harry Russell can control fractions, though the STYLE_FIT tag suggests this position may not be its most natural gear and it's one to respect rather than take at face value.

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a strong good-ground profile (14/15 similar-going runs placing) and a course win over the trip; natural hold-up mare who will need to be produced late, which is trickier in a race where the pace is unlikely to be searingly fast.

runners_data.name: Fierce
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves aboard a Paul Midgley sprinter whose best recent form (2nd and 3rd) came at 5f on good and standard; genuine hold-up style means it relies on others going hard enough — the controlled tempo here is not ideal for its finishing burst.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: 211 days off the track is a significant concern, and all five recent runs came on standard or soft going rather than good; a natural hold-up type whose off-the-pace style suits a strong pace that this race may not deliver.

runners_data.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners_data.note: Fahey four-year-old whose true hold-up style has been redistributed to midfield on the map — limited good-ground form (4/15 runs) and a tongue-tie add further caution; this is a race shape where its natural closing run is unlikely to materialise fully.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with a genuine hold-up profile pushed forward in the map due to overcrowding at the rear — best efforts on soft and standard going, and while it has a good-ground win in its history, the controlled tempo will blunt its late kick.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Faye McManoman takes the ride for Nigel Tinkler on this four-year-old who races prominently and handles good ground well (9/15 similar-going); a natural fit for the pace map position and one who benefits directly from the controlled front-running scenario.

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Dods seven-year-old who invariably comes from behind, with all recent runs over 6f rather than 5f — the step down in trip combined with a race shape that offers little late tempo makes this a difficult assignment, and its true hold-up style is squeezed in a field already crowded with closers.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up specialist carries a tongue-bar and a blinker flag, but its form over 6f is a concern at 5f; another genuine closer shuffled into a midfield map slot, facing the same late-pace problem as the other redistributed hold-up horses.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old races in a visor and has placed at 5f on good ground recently; Cam Hardie will look to track the leader from a prominent position, and the race shape sets this horse up nicely to make its challenge without requiring a dramatic finishing effort.

races.paceDynamic: Keldeo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on good ground over five furlongs at Beverley. Azuinthejungle and Bibendum will push forward to occupy prominent positions just behind, meaning the front three in the race map are reasonably settled, but the field holds more hold-up types than the track can accommodate — Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama, and Dream Deal are true closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would ideally like, compromising their natural finishing kick. With a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable rather than scorching tempo, the race is likely to develop into a test of straightforward speed rather than a sprint-finish cavalry charge from the rear. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and quicken over the final furlong, as true hold-up runners are unlikely to generate the momentum from the back they depend upon.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keldeo Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo leads unchallenged at a controlled tempo and prominent horses track comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Keldeo leads unchallenged at a controlled tempo and prominent horses track comfortably into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo's pace is slightly too strong and creates enough early tempo to set up a finish for the closers.
scenarios.body: If Keldeo's pace is slightly too strong and creates enough early tempo to set up a finish for the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Keldeo Front-Runs And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo's lead is fully uncontested and Ollie Pears's horse conserves enough to sprint clear from the front.
scenarios.body: If Keldeo's lead is fully uncontested and Ollie Pears's horse conserves enough to sprint clear from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Breaks Down, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for prominent positions disrupts the pace and fragments the field, creating a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: If early jostling for prominent positions disrupts the pace and fragments the field, creating a chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Keldeo's control of the tempo is the pivotal factor — if Harry Russell gets a soft lead, the entire race shape is set, but watch whether Azuinthejungle or Bibendum attempt to pressure him in the early stages, which would change the dynamics completely.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama, and Dream Deal — will all be racing closer than ideal; watch for traffic issues and crowding in the first two furlongs as genuine closers scramble for position.

Spirit Of Applause returns after 211 days off and has never run on good ground in its last five starts; significant fitness and going uncertainty makes this one to monitor in the market rather than trust at face value.

Miss Brazen's good-ground strike rate (14/15 placing runs on similar going) is the standout statistical edge in the field — if the pace does quicken enough to suit hold-up horses in the final furlong, it is the most likely beneficiary among the closers.

Bibendum wears a visor and Cam Hardie has a clear tactical brief to press forward — watch the early stalls to see whether it pushes up to challenge Keldeo's lead, as a two-horse breakaway at the front would significantly compress the race shape for the hold-up contingent.

races.name: Churchill Tyres Handicap

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 408-28 over 8f on Good, and Tom Eaves rides for a trainer who is 0/2 in the last 14 days; though mapped to midfield here, this horse's natural inclination is to race from the rear, which is a disadvantage in a race expected to develop into a sprint with no true pace to chase.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's yard is in form at 1/27 over 14 days and James Sullivan takes the ride on this ten-year-old who has placed twice from 15 runs on similar ground; finds itself in a midfield slot on the map yet instinctively prefers to race from off the pace, so a sprint finish suits only if it can secure an unimpeded run late.

runners_data.name: Anificas Beauty
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and has mixed form at various trips; Cian Horgan claims 5lb for a trainer at 0/2 in 14 days, and though the horse gravitates to the rear, its distance record includes a win at this sort of trip which provides some encouragement in what should be a slowly run race.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) partners this nine-year-old for the in-form Ruth Carr stable; the historical record shows five placed efforts from 15 runs on Good or Soft, and last ran 20 days ago — a genuine hold-up type who will need a strong sprint to develop late, but its consistency at 8f on Good gives it the most compelling profile in this confusing field.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Ran just 14 days ago and was a winner over 10f on Standard last time in that sequence; Cam Hardie rides for Mark Walford who sends out 1/19 recently — the horse has zero wins or places from seven runs on Good, which is a significant concern on today's Going, and its instinct to race from the back further complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's stable sends out five runners from 91 over 14 days; this nine-year-old wears a visor, last ran just 10 days ago, and placed twice from 15 similar-going runs including a second at 8f on Good — the horse settles deeply, which only works if the race develops a proper tempo, and in a sprint finish it will likely be doing its best work too late.

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream
runners_data.note: William Carson rides for a trainer who is 0/5 in the past 14 days, and form figures of 584D8/4 tell a tale of inconsistency; only three runs from seven have come on similar ground, and with no wins or placed efforts on Good, this five-year-old arrives without strong claims and its natural preference for the back of the field adds further risk in what looks a dawdle.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the mount — a significant booking — for Alan Brown who is 1/12 over 14 days; this four-year-old wears a visor, ran 10 days ago, and has one place from 15 runs on similar ground, with form figures of 95-707 showing limited consistency; instinctively races deep, and while McDonald's experience could place it handily in a slow-run race, the raw form is modest.

races.paceDynamic: Every single runner in this eight-horse field is catalogued as a hold-up type, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with a genuine inclination to lead — the race will almost certainly crawl into a sprint finish over Beverley's final two furlongs. On Good ground over 1m½f, the early gallop is likely to be a dawdle with jockeys reluctant to commit, creating a concertina-style race that compresses the field and turns the finish into a dash for the line. The absence of any pace will suit horses with a sharp late turn of foot or those able to travel prominently when the race unfolds slowly, rather than true hold-up artists who depend on a searching tempo. Horses that can race handy from a wide early pitch will be best placed when the sprint develops, while genuine backmarkers face the added difficulty of making up ground when no real gaps or gaps open up. Note also that several horses flagged as redistributed — including Can I Kiss You, Copper And Five, Little Ted, and Mavetheforcebewivu — are true hold-up types consigned to a midfield position on the map simply because the entire field shares that profile, so no single runner can genuinely be expected to be closer than any other from flagfall; the race shape will be determined purely by which jockeys show initiative in the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace-less Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner establishes any meaningful gallop and the field drifts en masse into a bunched sprint off a slow pace.
scenarios.body: If no runner establishes any meaningful gallop and the field drifts en masse into a bunched sprint off a slow pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Forcing Front-Runners Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If one or two jockeys decide to force the pace from the outset, nullifying the hold-up specialists.
scenarios.body: If one or two jockeys decide to force the pace from the outset, nullifying the hold-up specialists.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If horses drawn widest use their position to avoid early crowding and travel just off the crawl in an uncontested berth.
scenarios.body: If horses drawn widest use their position to avoid early crowding and travel just off the crawl in an uncontested berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine strong pace accidentally develops and the field strings out, opening ground for late runners.
scenarios.body: If a genuine strong pace accidentally develops and the field strings out, opening ground for late runners.

watchPoints.text: Hostelry — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall positions this horse prominently from the gate, as any horse that can travel just off the crawl rather than sit detached at the rear will hold a decisive advantage in what shapes as a sprint finish.

Copper And Five — James Sullivan's handling of this ten-year-old in the early stages is key; if Sullivan elects to nudge forward rather than settle, Copper And Five could steal a march on the hold-up pack before they realise the race is on.

Wicklow Way — Cam Hardie may be tempted to press on from the front given there is no natural leader, which would transform the race shape entirely; if Wicklow Way takes up the running, the whole scenario probability matrix shifts toward Scenario B.

Little Ted and Mavetheforcebewivu — both run in visors and both ran within the last 10 days; monitor their early positions, as freshness combined with headgear sometimes produces an uncharacteristically forward break that could seed a pace where none was expected.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for O'Meara/McDonald, ran only 6 days ago and arrives fit; holds Good-ground form at shorter trips but the step up to 1m2f here could stretch his stamina, and his sim-going record of just one place from 15 runs is a concern.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Has won and placed over 10f on Tapeta and won over 10f on Standard, so the step to 1m2f on Good is a genuine query; trainer Kellett has a quiet recent strike-rate (0/2 T14), though the 30-day break leaves him relatively fresh.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who placed over 10f on Good (2nd) and has Walford trainer-mate Sassy Glory as a stablemate; the 30-day absence is acceptable, but his sim-going record (1W from 11) suggests he finds this ground less productive than softer surfaces.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in this race; her STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that she has won from off the pace and may not be entirely natural up front, yet with no rival to challenge her she is likely to stride clear unchallenged through the early stages.

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: Placed over 12f on Good (4th) and won over 10f on Standard — the trip looks within range; wears a visor and has been seen just 12 days ago so arrives race-fit, though his sim-going record (0W1P from 15) is modest.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: A veteran nine-year-old who wears a hood (hg:p) and is a genuine hold-up type by nature; the trainer is in form (3/7 T14) and she ran just 12 days ago, but her true running style means she is unlikely to secure the prominent pitch the map shows her in, and five recent runs outside the top three on similar going dampens enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent-style filly who also wears a hood; Walford runs her alongside stablemate Quirke On Parole and she finished 4th over 12f on Good last time, which is directly relevant — her sim-going record (0W3P) suggests place rather than win claims.

runners_data.name: Regal Glory
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing hold-up type who naturally sits at the rear but is pushed into a midfield map position by the congestion; Roger Fell has three winners from 11 (T14) and she placed 4th over 12f on Good and 2nd over 14f — the trip is fine, though her STYLE_FIT (0.92) means an uncontested front-running shape may not suit.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Form reads 59-000 and she has failed to place in her last six runs, including three consecutive 0s; a genuine hold-up type whose best going record (0W0P on sim-going) offers little encouragement even if she does find her natural position at the rear.

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and blinkers (hg:tb) — significant headgear combination — yet has 0 wins and 0 places from 12 sim-going runs, making it difficult to identify a scenario where she wins; Brian Rothwell's runner is the rank outsider on pace-shape grounds.

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which is a critical concern in a race where the prominent horses may control the pace; a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map, his STYLE_FIT (0.92) and the fade flag together suggest this race shape does not set up for him despite the 49-day freshener.

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine challenger likely to push for the lead, she should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable, self-regulated tempo on Good ground at Beverley. Hijo De La Luna and Sassy Glory are the most likely horses to sit prominently just behind her, but neither has the profile to seriously pressurise the pace from the front. The majority of this field — Pisanello, Daring Leader, Quirke On Parole, Dandy's Angel, Regal Glory, Sweet Cicely, Rajawail, and Pureis King — are natural hold-up or midfield types, creating a compressed rearward cluster, and the field holds more true hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, with Pureis King, Dandy's Angel, and Regal Glory the most likely to be pushed out of their preferred positions. An uncontested, honest gallop on Good turf strongly favours the hold-up runners who can secure a clean passage and make up ground in the straight, but the overcrowded midfield means only those who find a clear run will benefit — mid-to-rear horses with strong finishing form on this going profile hold the tactical edge.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches — if she is allowed to dictate entirely unchallenged through the early stages, her ability to control tempo could make the race unwinnable for the hold-up pack regardless of how they travel.

Midfield congestion — with five horses tagged REDISTRIBUTED all clustering in a narrow central band, there is a genuine risk of bunching and blocked runs entering the straight; watch which jockeys elect to go wide early.

Pureis King — his flagged tendency to fade in the finish combined with a 49-day absence means he could carve through the midfield convincingly before stopping in the final furlong, potentially causing interference for closers behind him.

Daring Leader — Harry Russell is an apprentice booking on a horse with genuine win form over this sort of trip on Standard going; if the Good ground translates well, he could outrun his odds from the hold-up group.

Hijo De La Luna — 12 days between runs, visor retained, and a recent 4th over 12f on Good is the most directly relevant recent form line in the race; watch whether Aiden Brookes can hold a prominent pitch against Inspiring Speeches rather than being squeezed back.
